newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH C.BANK SEES NO FAST RATE CUT - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH C.BANK SEES NO FAST RATE CUT - PAPER.

text.p: Poland's central bank is reluctant to cut nominal interest rates despite a significantly lower trade deficit expected for February, the bank's deputy head told daily Rzeczpospolita in its Saturday edition.

"That doesn't mean, of course, that it's not necessary to worry about a negative foreign trade balance. From there comes our reluctance to lower nominal interest rates," Rzeczpospolita quoted Witold Kozinski as saying.

Over the last three months the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, has increased market interest rates and obligatory reserves to cool fast growing domestic demand, which it says could further widen the country's trade deficit.
On Friday the NBP announced that Poland's merchandise trade balance had reached $1.476 billion in January compared to $958 million in December and $661 million in January 1996.
January 1997's current account deficit was at $899 compared to $368 million in December and $139 million in January 1996.
Kozinski told the paper that the numbers were also not a signal for a radical change in exchange rate policy.
